title: Product-site module sheaves are diagram modules
statement: For small categories J,C, a topology K on C, a commutative ring sheaf O, the vertical topology T [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-topology], and a ring sheaf R whose underlying presheaf is the pullback of O from C, the category of module sheaves over R [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is equivalent to J-diagrams of module sheaves over O. The equivalence is restriction to the vertical slices on objects, restriction maps, horizontal maps and morphisms, with the heterogeneous equalities displayed in Lean. It is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits; for every j, its composite with evaluation preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

proof.text: Restrict a product module presheaf to each vertical slice with pushforward₀Obj. Horizontal restriction is linear because the coefficient restriction is the identity. Naturality and the product-arrow factorization assemble these into a functor to diagrams. Morphisms act componentwise.

proof.text: Uncurry a diagram of module sheaves: at a product object use its component module, and on arrows compose its horizontal map and vertical restriction. Prove semilinearity, composition, and naturality from the component module laws. The componentwise sheaf criterion proves the resulting additive presheaf is a sheaf.

proof.text: Build explicit unit and counit isomorphisms with identity section maps, using PresheafOfModules.isoMk. Product-arrow factorization proves their naturality and the triangle identity. These give an actual equivalence, and its object and morphism formulas follow by unfolding the constructions.

proof.text: An equivalence preserves finite limits and colimits, and finite-product preservation gives additivity. Mathlib forms module-sheaf colimits via sheafification and functor-category limits/colimits componentwise; evaluation therefore preserves finite limits and colimits. Compose these preservation instances with the equivalence.
